correctness.rationale: The Weyl-conjugation rank identity reduces the 81-projector span to the nonzero ambiguity support. The cyclotomic minimal-polynomial tests for orders 3 and 9 are exact, and a sign-ratio argument proves that a primitive modulation zero at any nonzero shift is equivalent to three-periodicity of the binary window. Three explicit 9-member positive-edge orbits classify all 27 nonconstant unit-shift events; the complete event intersection count gives exactly 117,81,54 nonperiodic windows at ranks 73,69,65 and four period-three windows at ranks 21 (three) and 9 (one). Both packaged integer and prime-modulus programs independently enumerate all 256 normalized windows. The modular test has an exact norm bound: 531613>9^6, so no nonzero cyclotomic integer of the form tested can falsely reduce to zero.

originality.rationale: The finding is the complete five-value binary nine-cycle projector-span rank spectrum with multiplicities, optimizer criterion, and explicit 27-pattern orbit proof. Classical Gabor/Weyl rank diagonalization and prime-power cyclotomic digit-fiber arithmetic are acknowledged as prior. The closest inspected prime-power note is for nonnegative rational generators and does not enumerate signed full-support nine-point windows; the prime phase-mask note assumes proper support and prime ambient order. Goldberger et al. study generic Gabor POVM rank and invariances but do not report the five precise binary rank classes. No equal or stronger published rank census was located in actual specific published-finding corpus and primary literature comparisons; unindexed equivalent binary-sequence results remain a priority risk.

value.rationale: Nine is the smallest odd prime-square cyclic ambient group; its binary sign alphabet exposes two genuinely distinct cyclotomic frequency orders. The complete intrinsic rank histogram is a natural phase-only matrix-recovery invariant; the theorem identifies a sharp 73-dimensional optimum, all 117 optimal windows via a four-event rule, and an exact structural four-rank gap rather than a merely reproducible point experiment. These values supply a concrete benchmark for minimum-alphabet Gabor intensity-design choices. No all-dimension or nonlinear-recovery theorem is necessary for the value of this naturally complete finite classification.
